meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (English common law as applied by the Supreme Court of Gibraltar, with local statutory enactments by the Gibraltar Parliament; offshore special territory characteristics)

Cayman Islands: Proceeds of Crime Act (2021 Revision); Anti-Money Laundering Regulations (2021 Revision); Beneficial Ownership Transparency Act, 2017 (as amended); Companies Act (2023 Revision); the Cayman Islands Competent Authority sanctions and beneficial ownership information-sharing framework.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 2014 (Gibraltar), ss. 5, 6, 7, 30, 39 and Schedule 1; Income Tax Act 2010 (Gibraltar), ss. 6-9 (non-residence taxation status); Economic Substance (Company Income Tax) Regulations 2019; Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 (Gibraltar) for AML/CDD filings. The vehicle is a Gibraltar company limited by shares structured as an exempted, non-tax-resident entity functionally equivalent to the Cayman Exempted Company template.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry, Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC), HM Government of Gibraltar
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form GIB-A1 - Application for Incorporation of a Company Limited by Shares, submitted with executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Gibraltar private limited company. At least one ordinary share of US$1.00 must be issued and fully paid at incorporation. There is no escrow account or paid-up capital deposit requirement under Gibraltar law; subscription proceeds may be paid in cash or satisfied by contributed assets and remain at the free disposal of the company upon registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY] LIMITED. Adopted on [DATE] by the subscriber and directors. RESOLVED THAT: (1) the subscription of one ordinary share of US$1.00 by the subscriber is approved and fully paid; (2) the registered office be and is hereby established at [address], Gibraltar, and [registered agent] is retained as registered agent; (3) [Director Name] is appointed Director and [Officer Name] Company Secretary, each authorised to execute and deliver all documents; (4) the Director is authorised to file the tax residence declaration, open bank and EMI accounts, and adopt operational merchant arrangements. Dated this [DATE].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation, Availability Search, and Corporate Compliance Pre-Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) - Registry E-Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the GFSC Companies Registry online portal and submit three proposed company names in the format '[Name] Limited'. Confirm that no restricted word (e.g., Bank, Insurance, Trust, Gaming) appears. Because the group name may contain 'Slots', file a brief statement confirming the activity is simulated social gaming only and not licensable gambling. Pay the name reservation fee and record the portal reference number.
required_dossiers: GIB-N1 Application for Name Reservation or portal submission screen
Written statement of non-licensed simulated social gaming activity
Certificate of incorporation of any parent entity (if applicable)
Identity and address verification of the requesting subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity or perceived gambling connotation, submit an alternative name within 7 calendar days through the same portal. The refusal letter does not invalidate the intended incorporation, and the first alternative name is searched without an additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, Execution, and Notarization of Constitutional Documents and Consent Forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (Gibraltar) and licensed corporate service provider / registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in line with the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 model articles. Execute the subscriber statement and consent to act forms. Arrange notarization of all execution pages; for a foreign corporate subscriber, obtain an apostilled power of attorney under the Hague Apostille Convention. Retain original executed documents for lodgement with the Companies Registry.
required_dossiers: Signed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Subscriber statement and incorporation declaration (Form GIB-A1)
Original or apostilled power of attorney for corporate subscriber
Certified passport copies of directors and beneficial owners
Proof of residential or business address
Source of funds statement and AML/KYC dossier
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notarial seal or apostille is queried, re-issue the affected pages with a fresh notarial certificate and, where necessary, re-execute the subscriber statement. The Registry accepts a corrected package without penalty provided it is re-lodged within 14 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing and Payment of Incorporation Fees with the Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the full incorporation package electronically through the GFSC Registry lodgement platform, including Form GIB-A1, executed Memorandum and Articles of Association, notices of registered office, consents to act, and the completed CDD file. Ensure all e-fields match the certified documents. Pay the statutory filing fee by bank transfer or card, then track the application using the assigned portal reference.
required_dossiers: Form GIB-A1 (Application for Incorporation)
Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Notice of registered office (Form GIB-RO)
Consents to act of director and company secretary
KYC/AML dossier of the ultimate beneficial owner
Proof of payment of filing fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a query under section 6 of the Companies Act 2014 or requests supplementary CDD under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015, respond within 14 days with amending documents; no additional refiling fee is charged for the correction. If incorporation is refused, remedy the stated grounds and resubmit within 30 days, with a refund of all fees except the name reservation charge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Gibraltar Tax Registration with Non-Residence Exemption
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry (GFSC) and Gibraltar Revenue Department (Income Tax and Economic Substance Unit)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, apply to the Gibraltar Revenue Department for a Taxpayer Reference Number. Submit a board-adopted declaration confirming that central management and control is exercised outside Gibraltar and that the company will not carry on trade in Gibraltar. File the initial nil-return and any required Economic Substance notification to confirm the entity is outside the scope of Gibraltar corporate tax.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Board resolution confirming tax residence and place of effective management
Company tax registration form and initial nil-return
Details of the registered office and registered agent
Beneficial ownership register opening entries
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Revenue Department queries the non-residence declaration, submit board minutes evidencing offshore decision-making and a written place-of-effective-management analysis. A formal representation may be filed within 30 days of the query without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance, Beneficial Ownership Filing, Data Protection Registration, and Bank/EMI Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry (BO filings), Gibraltar Regulatory Authority (GRA), and licensed commercial bank or electronic money institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the statutory registers (members, directors, charges, and persons with significant control), issue share certificates, and execute the registered office services agreement. File the Gibraltar register of beneficial owners through the Registry portal. Register the company as a data controller with the GRA under the Gibraltar Data Protection Act 2004 as applied by the UK GDPR framework. Complete enhanced onboarding with a licensed bank or EMI to support e-money accounts and merchant settlement for Apple IAP and Google Play Billing.
required_dossiers: Register of members and register of beneficial owners (PSC register)
Share certificates and share transfer forms
Data protection notification form and privacy policy
Bank or EMI account application with source of funds and business plan
Apple Developer Program and Google Play Console agreements for in-app billing rails
AML risk assessment (medium-risk enhanced) and compliance manual
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or EMI requires further information, provide board resolutions, transaction-flow diagrams, and certified proof of funds. Data protection registration deficiencies are cured by correcting and resubmitting the GRA form within 21 days. Where an account application is declined, a fresh application with a revised AML risk assessment and updated corporate structure chart may be filed without restriction.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for non-physical software publishing under ISIC 5820. Ancillary digital and consumer-protection registration is administered by the Gibraltar Regulatory Authority (GRA); the GFSC Gaming Division has no jurisdiction over simulated social casino software because no real-money gaming or cash-out functionality is offered.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required - confirmatory negative clearance for simulation-only social casino games under the Gambling Act 2005 (Gibraltar); no industrial or manufacturing permit applies to cloud-based software publishing.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environment, Sustainability, Heritage and Climate Change (DESHCC), HM Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no EIA screening or environmental statement required under the Town Planning (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 2000, as the activity is office-based digital publishing with no physical industrial installation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process discharges; office wastewater limited to domestic sewers; zero VOC process emissions; cloud infrastructure and game servers are hosted outside Gibraltar by ISO 14001-certified data centres; any end-of-life IT equipment must be disposed of through an approved Gibraltar WEEE collection operator, with no prohibited e-waste export.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate for the Gibraltar registered office premises issued by the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service; building structural load and occupancy certificate obtained by the landlord under the Town Planning (Buildings) Act; Employers' Health and Safety Statement filed under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2008 for any Gibraltar-based staff; remote and home-office workers are outside the scope of physical premises clearances.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Government of Gibraltar — Income Tax Office (ITO) under the Commissioner of Income Tax; corporate e-filing and tax registration portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/taxation (Corporation Tax e-Filing / e-Tax portal). Customs and excise indirect duties are administered by HM Customs Gibraltar (Her Majesty's Customs). The UK HMRC has no direct taxing authority over Gibraltar-resident or Gibraltar-registered taxpayers; however, UK VAT and Making Tax Digital rules can apply only if the entity has a separate UK establishment or is the deemed supplier, which is not the case where Apple IAP and Google Play Billing act as marketplace operators.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Cayman Exempted Company (ISIC 5820 social casino publishing) establishing a Gibraltar tax nexus: (1) Verify the Cayman entity's Certificate of Incorporation and Section 6 Tax Exemption Undertaking (Tax Concessions Act, Cap.152) remain valid; obtain a Cayman Certificate of Good Standing. (2) Appoint a Gibraltar-resident corporate service provider and tax representative; if a physical place of business is established, register the foreign company with the Gibraltar Companies Registry under the Companies Act 2014 to obtain a Gibraltar company/branch registration number. (3) Submit the ITO Corporate Taxpayer Registration form, attaching the Cayman constitutional documents, certificate of good standing, tax exemption undertaking, Gibraltar agent appointment, registered office address, and a business plan for the simulated social casino and virtual slots publishing activity, including target payment rails (Apple IAP, Google Play Billing). (4) The ITO issues a Gibraltar Tax Reference Number (TRN/UTR) upon acceptance. (5) Determine residence: a foreign-incorporated company is Gibraltar tax resident if central management and control is exercised in Gibraltar; if resident, Gibraltar Corporation Tax at 12.5% applies to worldwide profits; if non-resident, Gibraltar-source trading profits attributable to a Gibraltar permanent establishment (PE) remain taxable. (6) The TRN, together with the Cayman tax exemption undertaking, forms the KYC documentation pack for the UK-EMI/neo-bank account. Note: the pre-2010 Gibraltar 'exempt company' regime is abolished; no new statutory private tax exemption from Gibraltar Corporation Tax is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — The Cayman Exempted Company is statutorily exempt from Cayman Islands direct taxes (income, capital, withholding) for up to 30 years under the Section 6 Tax Exemption Undertaking, and is not subject to any Cayman economic substance requirement for pure holding/IP activity. For Gibraltar purposes, classification is dual: (a) non-resident company subject to territorial sourcing rules limited to Gibraltar-PE trading profits, or (b) resident company subject to entity-level Corporation Tax at 12.5% on worldwide profits if central management and control is exercised in Gibraltar. The entity is not fiscally transparent in either the Cayman Islands or Gibraltar; it is a distinct legal person with limited liability.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Available elections: (1) Cayman Islands Tax Exemption Undertaking (Section 6, Tax Concessions Act Cap.152) — one-time statutory election providing binding immunity from all Cayman direct taxes for 20 years, extendable by a further 10 years (maximum 30 years). (2) Gibraltar hybrid-mismatch election under the Taxation (Hybrid Mismatch) Rules (implementing EU ATAD 2, effective 1 January 2020) — if the Cayman entity is treated as fiscally transparent under another jurisdiction's rules (e.g., a US Form 8832 check-the-box election), the ITO must be notified and a mirroring adjustment applied to prevent deduction/non-inclusion outcomes. (3) US Form 8832 'check-the-box' election may be used by US owners to classify the Cayman entity as disregarded or partnership for US federal tax, but such election has no Gibraltar tax effect because Gibraltar Corporation Tax applies at the entity level without regard to foreign classification. (4) No Gibraltar 'check-the-box' regime exists; no statutory election permits pass-through treatment of a company for Gibraltar tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Gibraltar does not operate a VAT or GST system. Indirect taxation in Gibraltar consists of: (a) Import duties under the Gibraltar Customs Tariff (Customs Ordinance), (b) Excise duties on alcohol, tobacco and hydrocarbon oils, and (c) a remote gambling duty only for licensed real-money gambling operators under the Gambling Act 2005 — not applicable to simulated social casino with non-cashable virtual credits. For the app-store channel, UK VAT at 20% on UK consumer purchases is collected and remitted by Apple/Google as deemed marketplace suppliers under UK VATA 1994 Schedule 9A; EU consumer supplies are handled under the EU OSS/VAT regime by the platforms. The Cayman entity's developer receipts are outside the scope of Gibraltar indirect tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Gibraltar: nil threshold for customs registration — every importer of goods into Gibraltar must register with HM Customs Gibraltar; excise licensing applies only to alcohol/tobacco/fuel (not relevant). There is no VAT/GST registration threshold in Gibraltar because no VAT/GST exists. UK VAT: the Cayman entity is not required to register for UK VAT because Apple IAP and Google Play Billing are deemed suppliers of the digital services to consumers under UK VATA 1994 Schedule 9A; the entity's consideration attributable to the platforms is outside the scope. If the entity were ever to make direct B2C digital supplies in the UK outside a marketplace, the £85,000 UK VAT registration threshold (GBP) would apply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Gibraltar: no real-time fiscal clearance, no compulsory electronic invoicing, no digital stamping or SAF-T filing requirement; ordinary PDF/paper invoices satisfy Income Tax Act 2010 record-keeping obligations (minimum 6 years). UK indirect interface: if UK VAT registration were separately triggered (not applicable under the marketplace model), Making Tax Digital (MTD) would require functional compatible software for quarterly digital VAT returns — the UK has no PEPPOL e-invoicing mandate and no continuous transaction controls. Customs declarations into/out of Gibraltar and the UK use electronic SAD/C88 submissions via brokers; app-store transaction receipts (Apple/Google billing statements) serve as the principal evidential documents for platform fee reconciliation, AML/KYC and transfer-pricing audits.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Gibraltar itself has no VAT, so no Gibraltar zero-rating mechanism exists. For UK VAT purposes (if any UK registration becomes relevant): (a) physical exports of goods from the UK are zero-rated at 0% provided the goods leave the UK within the applicable time limits and the exporter retains prescribed evidence of export; (b) B2B supplies of digital services (including social casino publishing services) are outside the scope of UK VAT with the customer self-assessing reverse charge; (c) B2C digital services supplied to non-UK/non-EU consumers are outside the scope of UK VAT; for UK consumers the marketplace operators (Apple/Google) are the deemed suppliers and charge 20% UK VAT. The simulated social casino business under ISIC 5820 with virtual credits and no real-money wagering qualifies as a supply of digital entertainment services, not gambling services, and therefore no Gibraltar remote gambling duty or UK gambling tax applies. For export proceeds substantiation, this structure adopts a 180-day inward remittance benchmark (see below) to evidence the collection chain; no Gibraltar exchange-control statute imposes a fixed statutory repatriation deadline.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Official Customs Export Declaration (UK SAD/C88 or HM Customs Gibraltar export entry) with Unique Consignment Reference (UCR) evidencing the export movement
Transport document proving physical export: Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, CMR, or electronic export evidence issued by the carrier
Forex/inward remittance certificate or SWIFT MT103 bank statement evidencing collection of export sales proceeds within the 180-day repatriation benchmark
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or unsupported zero-rating/export claims: UK — civil penalty of up to 100% of the VAT evaded (VATA 1994 Schedule 24), conduct-based penalties (30% careless, 70% deliberate, 100% deliberate and concealed), default interest, and criminal prosecution for fraudulent evasion under VATA 1994 s.72 with imprisonment up to 7 years; customs export misdeclarations attract penalties under CEMA 1979, forfeiture and seizure of goods. Gibraltar — under the Income Tax Act 2010, knowingly false returns attract under-assessment penalties up to 100% of additional tax, statutory interest, and criminal sanctions; HM Customs Gibraltar may impose duty evasion penalties (up to treble the duty or £3,000 per offence) and confiscation. Retrospective clawback: the taxpayer must retain full export evidence and underlying app-store transaction records for at least 6 years (20 years where fraud or concealment is established); missing or fabricated evidence reopens the assessment period and reverses the zero-rating/outside-scope treatment with interest from the original due date.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Cayman Islands Monetary Authority (CIMA) — central bank and currency authority of the Cayman Islands, domicile of the Exempted Company; for the Gibraltar operational jurisdiction, the relevant authorities are the Government of Gibraltar (issuer of Gibraltar pound notes at par with sterling under the Currency Notes Act 1934) and the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC), which licenses and supervises banks and e-money institutions; ultimate sterling monetary policy is set by the Bank of England because the Gibraltar pound (GIP) is pegged 1:1 to GBP.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Both the Cayman Islands and Gibraltar maintain fully convertible currencies with no exchange controls. Cayman: capital and current-account items are freely convertible; the KYD/USD statutory peg of 1 USD = 0.80 KYD (i.e., 1 KYD = 1.25 USD) has been in force since 1974; profit and dividend remittance from an Exempted Company is unrestricted and is not subject to Central Bank approval or any withholding, because Cayman imposes no direct taxation. Gibraltar: GIP is freely convertible at par with GBP; there are no restrictions on capital-account transactions, profit repatriation, or dividend distribution; a Cayman Exempted Company that does not manage and control its affairs in Gibraltar remains outside Gibraltar income tax, so profit remittance through GBP/EUR/USD is unhindered. The practical hurdle is bank-level AML/CDD, not statutory FX control.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion obligation exists in the United Kingdom, Gibraltar, or the Cayman Islands. There is no prescribed timeline and no conversion ratio for export proceeds, including App-Store digital-content receipts; the company may lawfully retain USD, EUR, and GBP balances indefinitely. The former UK Exchange Control Act 1947 generally ceased to apply with effect from 1979, and neither the Cayman Islands Currency Law (2021 Revision) nor Gibraltar's Currency Notes Act imposes a surrender rule on software-publishing receivables. Banks apply only statistical reporting thresholds (e.g., UK International Transactions Reporting System/Balance of Payments reporting above GBP 50,000) and neither CIMA nor the GFSC requires repatriation or conversion of foreign-currency revenue.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for ancillary treasury functions; unsuitable as the sole primary settlement rail for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced social-casino publisher. Legal constraints: (i) EEA/UK e-money licences cannot automatically passport to a Cayman-incorporated account-holder, so most digital EMIs (Wise Business, Revolut Business, Airwallex) accept UK/Gibraltar-incorporated entities but exclude Cayman offshore companies from standard onboarding matrices; (ii) post-Brexit, an EEA EMI passport does not extend to Gibraltar, whereas UK-regulated EMIs have grandfathered access to Gibraltar and GFSC-licensed EMIs may passport into the UK under the Gibraltar Authorisation Regime; (iii) all major EMIs maintain prohibited-industry screens covering gambling, so the social-casino product must be underwritten as digital entertainment monetised exclusively through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing with no cash-out channel; (iv) EMI balances are not bank deposits and are not protected by the UK Financial Services Compensation Scheme or the Cayman Deposit Insurance Scheme, and EMIs do not provide credit or letter-of-credit services; (v) EMIs may become viable for FX conversion and low-value vendor pay-outs if the group interposes a UK operational subsidiary, but the Apple/Google USD settlement account must sit at a licensed bank with London or New York correspondent clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person interview mandate: mandatory for at least one director or the ultimate beneficial owner at GFSC-regulated Gibraltar banks and CIMA-regulated Cayman banks, given the Cayman-incorporated and gaming-adjacent profile. The acceptable standard is a physical due-diligence meeting at the bank's registered office (Gibraltar: the head office of Gibraltar International Bank or the Barclays branch at Europort; Cayman: the branch in Grand Cayman). Remote opening is permitted on a tightly-bounded basis where (i) the company has a Gibraltar-resident director and a GFSC-licensed corporate service provider; (ii) a senior compliance officer completes a live video interview with digital identity verification through an ISO 27001-certified provider; and (iii) notarised passport copies, bank references, and certified extracts of the register of directors and members are delivered through a recognised professional intermediary. For the Cayman entity, remote onboarding through a CIMA-regulated introducer is possible, but for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced classification the bank will usually demand a physical UBO or director appearance at least once within the first twelve months to recertify the file.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Simulated-gambling typology: the bank's AML model flags slot-style game mechanics as gambling-linked activity under FATF casino and online-gambling risk categories, notwithstanding the absence of real-money wagering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier bundle: (a) UK legal opinion under Gambling Act 2005 sections 3 and 6 confirming the product offers no prize in money or money's worth and no cash-out or conversion of virtual chips; (b) written confirmation that the app complies with Apple App Store Review Guideline 4.9 and Google Play Real-Money Gambling policy, neither of which permits real-money casino functionality; (c) product screenshots and user-flow diagrams showing chips are non-tradeable and non-convertible; (d) a written AML/economic-risk assessment classifying the business as low-risk digital entertainment; (e) copies of Apple IAP and Google Play Billing transaction records proving the only monetisation is via the storefronts' payment rails; (f) a supplementary legal certification from a Gibraltar 'A-list' law firm that no gambling licence is required under Gibraltar's online-gambling regulations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore-shell red flag: Cayman Exempted Company with nil minimum capital, non-resident ownership, and no apparent economic footprint is treated as a potential conduit for money laundering or tax evasion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier bundle: (a) certificate of incorporation and registered-office certificate from a licensed Cayman fiduciary; (b) Cayman Economic Substance Notice and self-assessment showing the entity is either a pure equity-holding or tax-exempt zone company as applicable; (c) proof of Gibraltar operating substance — lease agreement, local payroll records, annual returns, and appointment of a Gibraltar-resident director; (d) updated register of directors, members, and persons with significant control showing nationality and full tax residence details; (e) three-year business plan with headcount, app-development budgets, and projected App-Store receipts; (f) statutory declarations of each UBO together with source-of-funds statements certified by an attorney-at-law admitted in Gibraltar or the Cayman Islands.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cayman Exempted Company Annual Return and Government Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 January for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of 10% per month on unpaid fee; failure for 3 consecutive years may result in automatic strike-off and dissolution of the Cayman entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar External Company Annual Return (Form for Overseas/External Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 months of the date of registration in Gibraltar, and annually thereafter on the same return date (or within 42 days of each anniversary)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Escalating late filing penalties up to GBP 1,000; continued default may lead to removal of the Gibraltar registration and prohibition from operating a place of business.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Annual Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Register Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Companies Registry (via Authorised Resident Agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days following the company's annual return date (rolling anniversary of Gibraltar registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil penalties up to GBP 10,000, daily default fines, and potential criminal sanctions for non-compliance; in addition, the company may be prevented from filing and struck off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is mandatory for either the Cayman exempted company or the Gibraltar-registered external company under this structure. An audit is compulsory only for regulated classes (bank, insurance, fiduciary, fund) or if the parent has a listing requiring IFRS/US GAAP audited consolidation. Low-risk social casino publishing does not trigger audit requirements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: For any local statutory financial information required in Gibraltar, IFRS as adopted by the UK/Gibraltar applies. The Cayman parent may prepare accounts under IFRS, US GAAP, or a permitted Cayman GAAP basis; no filing of accounts with the Cayman Registrar is required.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Gibraltar Beneficial Ownership (Residential Agents) Regulations, the external company must maintain a Nigerian-style beneficial ownership register at its registered office, and any transfer of shares or membership changes in the Cayman parent must be notified to the Gibraltar resident agent within 14 days. The resident agent files an annual confirmation of the UBO register with the Gibraltar Companies Registry within 30 days of the statutory return date, even if no shareholding movement has occurred.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 1,200 – 3,500 (Cayman registered office and Gibraltar resident agent combined)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0 (no statutory audit required); voluntary audit market range 4,000 – 9,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holidays; foreign-source dividend exemption and capital gains exemption are available under the Income Tax Ordinance; the Cayman Exempted Company remains fully tax-exempt in its home territory, but Gibraltar tax at 10% applies to Gibraltar-source chargeable profits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Gibraltar Company Tax Return (Form GCT-100) filed through the E-Tax Online portal of the Gibraltar Tax & Customs Authority
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 30 days of the issue of the Notice of Assessment or by the statutory filing date of 30 November following the accounting period, whichever is earlier

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identity and full legal name
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident Cayman Exempted Company, state the company name, registered address in Cayman, and Gibraltar tax reference number
Mark 'Non-Resident' if management and control are exercised outside Gibraltar, and provide evidence of foreign tax residence

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Chargeable profits from Gibraltar source trading
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only profits attributable to a Gibraltar permanent establishment; for pure foreign digital platform income, enter nil if no PE in Gibraltar
For a Cayman Exempted Company, list dividends or capital gains from foreign subsidiaries; attach proof of foreign tax paid or exemption certificate

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments for capital allowances and disallowed expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with a Gibraltar permanent establishment must add back non-deductible entertainment and depreciation in line with Gibraltar tax law
Summarise adjusted chargeable profits; if nil, still complete all boxes for formal filing
Calculate 10% of chargeable profits less any double taxation relief; attach treaty claim if applicable
Sign as director of the Cayman Exempted Company, providing power of attorney if a UK/Gibraltar agent signs

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of GIP 10 per day up to GIP 1,000, plus 10% of tax charged for failure to notify chargeability; a further GIP 100 per day after a three-month notice; deliberate non-filing attracts a penalty of up to 100% of the tax underpaid and potential criminal prosecution under the Income Tax Ordinance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% (Gibraltar imposes no domestic withholding tax on dividends paid to non-residents)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Gibraltar's limited double taxation agreement network includes the UK. To claim treaty benefits, a non-resident recipient must file a Certificate of Tax Residence from the jurisdiction of residence (e.g., Cayman Islands: a Certificate of Tax Exempt Status) with the Gibraltar Tax & Customs Authority prior to payment; the payer may retain a copy for six years. Since Gibraltar does not levy withholding tax at source, treaty relief is primarily relevant for confirming residency and avoiding assessment for tax residents.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% statutory rate applies to royalties and interest paid by Gibraltar entities to non-residents; treaty rates would also be 0% under the UK-Gibraltar DTA and other agreements, following OECD minimum standards on exchange of information.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory where related-party transactions exceed GIP 1,500,000 annually; Master File is required where total consolidated group revenue exceeds GIP 50,000,000 and the Gibraltar entity's related-party transactions exceed GIP 1,500,000
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Gibraltar Economic Substance Act 2018 (as updated in 2021) applies to relevant activities, including IP holding and financing. A Cayman Exempted Company carrying on simulated social casino publishing through Gibraltar must demonstrate economic substance in Gibraltar if it purports to be tax resident there; if it is not tax resident, it must provide a CPA-approved conclusion of management and control outside Gibraltar.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating Apple IAP and Google Play Billing revenue derived from Gibraltar-based customers in the GCT-100 return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty up to 100% of the evaded tax; criminal fine up to GIP 100,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years under the Income Tax Ordinance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the restitution of evaded tax; criminal conviction triggers travel bans and asset freezing under the Misuse of Drugs Act (criminal asset recovery) and fraud offences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Cayman Exempted Company with no physical office, no Gibraltar employees, and no real economic activity, while using the Gibraltar mailing address to access exclusive treaty benefits or to claim non-resident status without substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of non-resident status; re-assessment of all Israel? Actually Gibraltar-source income taxed at 10%; annual penalty of GIP 10,000 for false statements; cancellation of tax reference and business registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face disqualification orders, civil recovery of unpaid taxes, and a possible fine of up to GIP 50,000 for knowingly permitting a shell structure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing social casino deposits without conducting enhanced due diligence on Apple IAP and Google Play Billing flows, or ignoring transactions originating from unregulated gambling wallets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 and Financial Action Task Force recommendations, a penalty of up to GIP 500,000 and up to 7 years imprisonment for money laundering offences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for failing to file suspicious activity reports with the Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit; travel bans can be imposed pending investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring a royalty payment from the Gibraltar operating company to a related Cayman IP holding company at a non-arm's length mark‑up to erode the Gibraltar taxable base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Commissioner of Income Tax will impose an arm's length adjustment, added interest at 6% per annum, and a tax-geared penalty of up to 100% of understated tax for gross negligence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve the pricing unjustifiably are personally liable for the penalty portion, and may be subject to civil proceedings for misfeasance in Cayman or Gibraltar.
